text: Princess Bathildis of Anhalt-Dessau (German: Prinzessin Bathildis Amalgunde von Anhalt-Dessau; 29 December 1837 – 10 February 1902) was a member of the House of Anhalt by birth and held the title of Princess of Anhalt-Dessau. Through her marriage to Prince William of Schaumburg-Lippe, she became a Princess of Schaumburg-Lippe. She was born in Dessau, Anhalt-Dessau, as the second child of Prince Frederick Augustus of Anhalt-Dessau, son of Frederick, Hereditary Prince of Anhalt-Dessau, and Landgravine Amalie of Hesse-Homburg, and Princess Marie Luise Charlotte of Hesse-Kassel, daughter of Landgrave William of Hesse-Kassel and Princess Charlotte of Denmark. She was the younger sister of Grand Duchess Adelaide of Luxembourg. On 30 May 1862 in Dessau, she married Prince William of Schaumburg-Lippe, the seventh child and third son of George William, Prince of Schaumburg-Lippe, and Princess Ida of Waldeck and Pyrmont. The couple had eight children. Bathildis died on 10 February 1902 at Náchod Castle, Kingdom of Bohemia (now the Czech Republic), at the age of 64. Her body was buried alongside her husband Friedrich in a Waldeck family Crypt in Rhoden, Harz, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany.
